excerpt: Assembly is a CRM and branded client portal for service firms, and Assembly Studio adds an AI app builder that creates custom client apps inside your workspace from a description. Pricing, alternatives and launch details.
content:
Assembly is a platform for service businesses such as accounting, consulting and creative firms. It combines a CRM with a branded client experience on your own domain, where clients can message your team, share files, sign contracts and pay, plus more than 30 ready-made apps for intake, onboarding, proposals, payments and project tracking.

Assembly Studio, the AI app builder launched on Product Hunt, covers whatever those apps don't. You describe the app you need, review and approve the plan the builder proposes, and it builds the app into your workspace with sign-in, permissions and your branding already in place, then you keep refining it by chat. Assembly says the security pieces (sign-in, permissions and data isolation) are platform infrastructure rather than AI-generated code, that each app runs in its own sandbox and that it holds SOC 2 Type II. Apps can connect to tools such as Slack, Notion, Google Drive, HubSpot and Airtable. According to its AI policy, the builder uses providers including Anthropic and OpenAI, and Assembly does not use your prompts or data to train models. The company is Copilot Platforms Inc., doing business as Assembly. Studio launched on 12 August 2026, Assembly's third Product Hunt launch, and finished #4 for the day with 254 points.

We have not tested Assembly ourselves. This page brings together its official site, its Product Hunt page and the public pages of the products it is compared with, and says where each fact comes from.

profile.starts_at: Free plan; paid from $29/month billed annually
profile.summary_short: Client portal and CRM for service firms with an AI builder for custom client apps

gallery.alt: Assembly app builder asking 'what app will you add?', with suggested apps including a progress tracker, proposal builder and onboarding wizard
Assembly prompt box asking to build a white-labelled client project tracker, under the line 'Stop paying for expensive software. Clone it instead.'
Assembly connectors settings listing Slack, Notion, Google Drive, Airtable, HubSpot, Typeform, OneDrive, Dropbox and LinkedIn

fit: run a service firm (accounting, consulting, agency) and want clients to message, share files, sign and pay in one branded place
need a custom client-facing tool, like an intake form or project tracker, without hiring a developer
need HIPAA support: the Advanced plan offers a BAA
not_fit: sell to consumers: Assembly's terms say the service is for business activity only
want a general-purpose app builder for public websites, since apps live inside your Assembly workspace
need a custom domain on a small budget: custom domains start on the Professional plan

pricing.intro: Assembly has a free-forever plan and paid plans. The plan cards show prices billed annually, in US dollars; monthly billing costs more (the pricing page's FAQ gives Starter as $29/month billed annually vs $49 billed monthly).

plans.name: Free
plans.detail: 5 active contacts, 1 internal user, 50 build credits a month, up to 3 apps, CRM, client experience, messaging and payments

plans.name: Starter
plans.detail: Billed annually. 50 active contacts, 1 user, 200 build credits a month, API and MCP connector

plans.name: Professional
plans.detail: Billed annually. 500 active contacts, 3 users, 200 build credits a month, custom domains, no Assembly badge, automation builder, AI model selection

plans.name: Advanced
plans.detail: Billed annually. Unlimited contacts, 5 users, 200 build credits a month, audit log, enforced MFA, HIPAA (BAA), priority call support

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.detail: Unlimited users, contacts and apps, custom SSO, volume build credits

notes: Build credits are only used when the builder creates or edits an app; using live apps is free, and planning or failed builds cost nothing.
Extra build credits cost $0.60 each on paid plans. Unused credits roll over for one more month.
The Free plan includes 3 apps and paid plans include 5; extra apps cost $5/month each on any paid plan.

alternatives.intro: These are products Product Hunt lists as alternatives. Review scores are Product Hunt users' own.

items.name: Formaloo
items.what: No-code forms, client portals, PDF builder and approval workflows
items.difference: Also builds client portals without code, but from forms and workflows rather than an AI builder plus CRM.

items.name: HubSpot
items.what: Marketing, sales and service platform with a free CRM
items.starts_at: Free tools; see its pricing page
items.difference: A much broader CRM and marketing suite. Assembly centres on the client-facing portal for service firms.

items.name: folk
items.difference: A sales CRM, with no branded client portal or payments.

alternatives.more: Product Hunt also lists Copilot and Uspacy as alternatives.

x.none: We did not check X for this profile.

faq.a: Assembly's AI app builder. You describe an app, approve the plan and it builds the app into your Assembly workspace with sign-in, permissions and branding. It launched on Product Hunt on 12 August 2026.
A CRM and branded client portal for service businesses, where clients can message, share files, sign contracts and pay, with 30+ ready-made apps.
There is a free plan. Paid plans billed annually are $29 a month (Starter), $99 (Professional) and $499 (Advanced), with Enterprise on request.
Credits used when the builder creates or edits an app. A typical app takes a few dozen credits; using live apps uses none. Extra credits cost $0.60 each.

faq.q: Does Assembly train AI on my data?
faq.a: Its AI policy says Assembly does not use prompts, inputs or outputs from its AI features and MCP connections to train any AI model.
Assembly says sign-in, permissions and data isolation are built into the platform, each app runs in its own sandbox, and it is SOC 2 Type II certified.
